primitives.name: OSS Leverage Conversion Operator
primitives.verbatim_quote: ## Why It Matters This improves decision quality, revenue, speed, support, retention, trust, or cost savings by converting open-source leverage into a bounded GSE workflow.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: OSS_study: dimensionless (research artifact count); License_allowed: dimensionless (binary compliance flag); GSE_workflow: dimensionless (bounded workflow unit); bounded(·): projection operator; compliant(·): filter operator; ⊗: tensor product combining study and compliance
primitives.assumptions: Open-source repos (AnythingLLM, Hoppscotch) provide studyable APIs/docs; license terms permit study, API use, self-hosted lab, original integration code; conversion preserves GSE architectural invariants
primitives.breakdown_regime: License violation (AGPL/MPL/custom without approval); production data leakage; unbounded workflow scope creep; unapproved app-code modification

layer2.mapping: Isomorphic to GSI evidence-to-posterior update where OSS study is evidence, license compliance is prior support, bounded workflow is posterior; GSE state-transition from research to approved workflow mirrors Bayesian update with hard constraints
layer2.telemetry: Count of OSS features mapped to GSE workflow steps; license compliance audit pass rate; sandbox-to-production transition latency

primitives.name: Isolation Boundary Enforcement Operator
primitives.verbatim_quote: Start in docs or a sandbox and only move into app code after explicit approval.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: State_docs/sandbox: dimensionless (isolated environment state); State_app-code: dimensionless (production-adjacent state); approval: binary gate (0/1); transition(·): state morphism; ℐ: isolation monad enforcing boundary
primitives.assumptions: Docs/sandbox environments contain no production secrets, PII, payment data, or deploy config; explicit approval is a discrete event; rollback to docs/sandbox is always possible
primitives.breakdown_regime: Implicit approval bypass; sandbox contamination with production data; missing rollback documentation; approval gate compromise

layer2.mapping: Derives GSE situational reasoning kernel: current state = docs/sandbox; next state = app-code iff approval predicate true; security boundary defines invariant subspace where secrets/PII/production keys have zero projection
layer2.telemetry: Approval gate invocation count; sandbox contamination incidents; rollback execution time; production-secret exposure events (target: 0)

primitives.name: Legal License Compliance Filter
primitives.verbatim_quote: Disallowed: copying source code or UI into GSE, white-labeling restricted projects, or modifying AGPL/MPL/custom-license code without legal approval.
primitives.latex: \mathcal{C}: \text{Action} \to \{0,1\} \quad \mathcal{C}(a) = \mathbb{1}[a \in \text{Allowed}] \quad \text{Allowed} = \{\text{study docs, use APIs, self-host lab, write original integration}\}
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: Action: dimensionless (candidate operation); Allowed: set of permitted actions (cardinality 4); 𝒞(a): indicator function (0=disallowed, 1=allowed); 𝕀[·]: Iverson bracket; legal_approval: binary predicate for AGPL/MPL/custom modifications
primitives.assumptions: License categories (MIT, AGPL, MPL, custom) are known; legal approval process exists for restricted modifications; self-hosted lab is network-isolated
primitives.breakdown_regime: Unclassified license ambiguity; white-labeling detection failure; legal approval latency exceeding sprint cadence; upstream license change without notice

layer2.mapping: Isomorphic to GSI conformal prediction compliance set: allowed actions form prediction set with 100% coverage guarantee; disallowed actions are rejected hypotheses; legal approval expands set conditionally
layer2.telemetry: License classification accuracy; legal approval turnaround time; disallowed-action detection rate; compliance audit findings

primitives.name: Rollback Reversibility Operator
primitives.verbatim_quote: Avoid `.env*`, Stripe/billing code, launch gates, production deploy config, and unrelated app files.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: Artifact_card-specific: dimensionless (file/branch count); delete(·): file removal operator; revert(·): git branch reset operator; ∅: empty artifact set; ℛ ∘ ℒ = id_docs: round-trip identity on docs state
primitives.assumptions: Card-specific artifacts are disjoint from production; isolated branch contains no merged production changes; docs-first start guarantees zero production dependency
primitives.breakdown_regime: Artifact misidentification (deleting non-card files); branch contamination with production merges; docs-first violation creating production coupling; rollback execution failure

layer2.mapping: Derives GSE state-transition reversibility kernel: forward transition ℒ (docs→workflow) has left-inverse ℛ; conformal risk bound = 0 for production impact; theory-of-mind models reviewer as adversarial auditor verifying ℛ ∘ ℒ = id
layer2.telemetry: Rollback drill success rate; artifact isolation verification; branch purity check; production impact incidents (target: 0)

Duality: ℒ expands scope (research→workflow), ℛ contracts (workflow→docs). Failure modes are singularities where boundaries dissolve: license violation breaks 𝒞, approval bypass breaks ℐ, production coupling breaks ℛ. The system is a category with objects = {docs, sandbox, app-code, production} and morphisms = {ℒ, ℐ, 𝒞, ℛ} where production is a terminal object with no inbound morphisms from this card. GSE/GSI mapping: ℒ ≈ Bayesian evidence update, ℐ ≈ state-transition guard, 𝒞 ≈ conformal compliance set, ℛ ≈ risk-bound reversal.
